content_metadata.description: This educational video uses various hands-on experiments and visual aids to explain the concept of pressure, force, and contact area. Through practical demonstrations involving common objects, the video aims to provide a clear understanding of how pressure operates in everyday life and science.

qAndA.answer: If you hammer a nail with the head at the bottom, it won't pierce through the wood because the force applied will be distributed over a larger area, thus reducing the pressure on the surface.
qAndA.question: What happens if you hammer a nail with the head at the bottom?

qAndA.answer: We use knives to cut tomatoes because they have a sharp edge, which increases the pressure on the tomato's surface allowing it to be cut with less force.
qAndA.question: Why do we use knives to cut tomatoes?

qAndA.answer: The experiment with the flour was used to empirically demonstrate that the pressure exerted by an object depends on its weight and the contact area. When the box is placed horizontally, the weight is distributed over a larger area, so the pressure is less. But when it is placed vertically, the same weight is concentrated over a smaller area, hence increasing the pressure on the surface, making the mark on the flour deeper.
qAndA.question: What was the experiment with the flour about?

qAndA.answer: The mark is deeper when the box is placed vertically because the weight of the box is concentrated over a smaller area, so the pressure on the surface is larger. This larger pressure makes the box sink deeper into the flour, thus making the mark deeper
qAndA.question: Why is the mark on the flour deeper when the box is vertical compared to when it is horizontal?

qAndA.answer: The units of pressure are Newtons per meter squared.
qAndA.question: What are the units of pressure?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Have you ever hammered a nail like this?
No right, you must have hammered a nail like this.
Only then it can punch you through the wood.
But why?
You might say that this end is more pointy.
Let's take one more example.
We use knives to chop tomatoes right.
But have you ever thought of chopping tomatoes with your finger?
No right, and you might say well the finger is not as sharp as a knife.
We will answer these questions in more detail with the help of an activity.
So for this activity I have some flour and this box with some chalks in it.
I will place some blocks like this horizontally and when I do that I see that it has left
a mark on the flour and there is this much depth to the mark.
Now I will leave the box like this that is vertically.
And I again see that the box has left a mark on the flour.
Now there is this much depth to the mark.
In which case is a depth more?
If we compare these two cases we can see the mark has a greater depth in this case.
Why did that happen?
Let's dive deeper.
Now every object has a weight of its own right like the box of chalks.
When the box was kept horizontally the force was divided over a larger area and when
it was kept vertically it was divided over a smaller area.
Now because the same force of weight was divided over a larger area in the case on the left
the amount of force that appears or acts on any one point on the flour is very small.
For the case on the right the amount of force that appears or acts on any one point on
the flour is larger.
So if we have the same force then the depth of the mark is less when the box was kept horizontal
and the depth of the mark is more when the box was kept vertical.
It matters how concentrated the force is.
Same force is divided over a larger area in the first case so it is not that concentrated.
But when the same force is divided over a smaller area then it is more concentrated and
this is what we call pressure.
Pressure can be thought of as how concentrated your force is.
We can even calculate pressure.
Well just like we saw that we are basically calculating how much force gets divided over
the area.
Mathematically also pressure that is P is calculated as the force divided by the area.
And its units will be Newton per meter square.
So in the first case when the area was very large the pressure was small.
But in the second case when the area was small the pressure became large.
Now let's come back to our original question.
Why do we hammer a nail with a pointy end at the bottom?
Well then force is concentrated over a very tiny area.
But in the case on the right the same force is concentrated over a larger area.
And as a result if you now compare the amount of force that appears on the same spot as
before the force has reduced a lot right because it got divided.
The contact area was very small in the first case so the pressure was very high and the
contact area was large in the second case.
So the pressure is very low.
Similarly when you use a knife and put a force then all the force gets concentrated into
a very tiny area because the knife is very sharp.
So that means the tomato experiences a large pressure.
But because your finger is not so sharp the base area of a finger is so wide at least
compared to the knife that entire force gets divided over a larger area.
And as a result the amount of force that appears on the same slice of tomato as before is
small.
So now the tomato experience is less pressure.
